To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novel polycarbo substituted 4-anilines-quinazolines have been synthesized, and some of these compounds have shown promising in vitro cytotoxic activity against human breast adenocarconma, human cervical cancer and human lung cancer cell lines.
we developed a one-pot three step reaction sequence for the synthesis of novel, unsymmetrical polylcarbon-substituted 2-aryl 4-anilnoquinazoline derivatives.
the polycarbo-functionalized 4-anilinosubstituted quinazolines were synthesized and evaluated for potential cytostatic and cytotoxic activity in three human cancer cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of novel polycarbo- substituted anilinoquinazoline derivatives and the evaluation of their potential to inhibit the growth of three cancer cell lines and to induce apoptosis and necrosis.

the development of a new class of polycarbo substituted 4-(arylamino)quinoline-2-carboxamides and the investigation of their cytotoxic properties against three human cancer cell lines, MCF-7, HeLa and A549.
the synthesis and in vitro cytotoxicity evaluation of a series of novel 2,2′,2″-polycarbo-substuted 4-anilinquinazolines and their potential to induce apoptosis or necrosis in cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compounds 2c and 3c are potential apoptosis inducers and compound 7a is a potential apoptosis inducer and/or necrotor.
compounds 2c and 3c are potential apoptosis inducers, while compound 7a has a necrotic effect.
compounds 3c, and 7a are more potent than compounds 2c in inducing necrosis in the cell membrane alteration assay, whereas compounds 2c and 3c are more potent in inducing caspase- 3 activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compounds 2c and 3c are more selective against MCF-7 cell lines than Hela or A549 cell lines.
the cytotoxicity of these novel 4-anilinesquinazolines was dependent on the nature of the cross-coupling partners used for the double carbon–carbon bond formations.
compounds 3c, and 7a are potential candidates for further investigation as anticancer agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polycarbo-functionalization of 4-anilines can lead to compounds with potential for cytotoxicity against cancer cell lines.
the 4-(aryl)amino-quinazolines are potential candidates for further development as cytotoxic anticancer agents.
polycarbo-functionalised 4-anilnoquinazolines can be synthesised via a three-step one-pot reaction sequence.
